forcing_mechanism.evidence: National rules were due by 7 June 2026. Employers with 150-249 workers first report pay gaps by 7 June 2027, backed by national fines.

findable.evidence: SIRENE and France Travail ads name French companies with NAF code and staff band. The catalogue holds no Spanish dataset.

early.evidence: Job ads update live and SIRENE monthly, so both list firms before the 7 June 2027 first reporting deadline.

gap_evidence.evidence: France Travail ads carry a salary field, but employers may give pay before the interview or otherwise, so an empty field proves nothing.

crowding.evidence: Pay-gap reporting by sex applies to all private employers from 150 workers, so every payroll and HR vendor can pitch the same report.

list_recipes.filter: codeNAF 55, 56, 47 or 41-43; trancheEffectifEtab 10-249 staff; dateCreation after 7 June 2026
list_recipes.gap_evidence: salaire field empty or without an amount or range
list_recipes.metric: share of the company's live ads without a pay amount or range
list_recipes.caveat: Employers may give pay information before the interview or otherwise, so an ad without pay does not prove non-compliance.

list_recipes.filter: activitePrincipale NAF 55, 56, 47 or 41-43; trancheEffectifs bands covering 150-249 staff
list_recipes.gap_evidence: none in the register; the size band only marks the first reporting duty due 7 June 2027
list_recipes.caveat: SIRENE shows sector and size only, not whether a company has prepared its pay gap report.
